summary: IRCC requires strict compliance for non-English and non-French supporting documents submitted in Express Entry and permanent residence applications. Mandatory standards mandate that translations must be completed by a certified translator in good standing (bearing their official stamp, seal, and registration number) or accompanied by a sworn translator affidavit executed before an authorized commissioner of oaths. Common failure modes causing application rejections, completeness check failures, or Procedural Fairness Letters (PFL) include using non-certified translators without an affidavit, relying on family members for translation, submitting incomplete page translations that omit stamps or annotations, and missing certified stamps or credentials.

failure_modes.title: Translation Completed by Uncertified Translator Without Sworn Affidavit
failure_modes.description: The submitted translation was performed by a translator who is not a certified member of a recognized provincial or national translation association, and the applicant failed to include a sworn affidavit from the translator attesting to language proficiency and accuracy executed before a commissioner authorized to administer oaths.
failure_modes.supporting_excerpt: Unless we tell you otherwise, all supporting documents must be in English or French. If it is not in English or French, you must send it with: the English or French translation and an affidavit from the person who completed the translation and a certified photocopy of the original document
failure_modes.remediation_hypothesis: Obtain a sworn affidavit signed by the non-certified translator in front of an authorized commissioner for taking affidavits, or re-translate the document using a certified translator affiliated with a recognized Canadian translation body.

failure_modes.title: Translation Prepared by Applicant or Family Member
failure_modes.description: The document translation was completed by the applicant themselves or an immediate family member (e.g., spouse, parent, sibling, child), which violates explicit IRCC regulations even if the relative is a professional or certified translator.
failure_modes.supporting_excerpt: Yes. If your documents are not in English or French, you must send a translation from a certified translator with your application. We don’t accept translations by family members.
failure_modes.remediation_hypothesis: Re-translate the document using an independent third-party certified translator who has no personal or familial relationship to the applicant.

failure_modes.title: Incomplete Translation Omitting Stamps, Marginalia, or Back Pages
failure_modes.description: The translated document omits portions of the original source document, such as government seals, registrar stamps, reverse-side endorsements, marginal notes, or attached pages, violating IRCC word-for-word completeness standards.
failure_modes.supporting_excerpt: Any document that is not in English or French must be accompanied by a certified translation. You must include a scan of both the original document and the complete translation.
failure_modes.remediation_hypothesis: Obtain a comprehensive, unabridged translation covering all text, stamps, signatures, marginalia, and back-page notations present on the source document.

failure_modes.title: Missing Official Stamp or Seal of Recognized Certified Translator
failure_modes.description: The translation claims to be certified but lacks the official stamp, seal, or membership credentials of a recognized provincial or territorial organization of translators (such as ATIO, STIBC, OTTIAQ), preventing IRCC officers from verifying the translator's professional certification status.
failure_modes.supporting_excerpt: An affidavit for a translation is a document that says the translation is a true and accurate version of the original text. The translator swears that their translation is a true and accurate representation of the contents of the original document.
failure_modes.remediation_hypothesis: Provide a re-issued translation bearing the official seal/stamp and membership number of a certified translator in good standing with a recognized professional translation body.
